newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Early frosts forecast in Brazil's far south states.
newsitem.headline: Early frosts forecast in Brazil's far south states.

text.p: This weekend should see the first light frosts of the year in the highland areas of Brazil's southern Rio Grande do Sul and Santa Catarina states, according to independent forecasters Somar Meteorologia.
"These are the first frosts of the year and they are around 15 days earlier than usual," said forecaster Marcos Massari.
There is no frost threat however for the country's more northern coffee regions where colder weather normally only starts to pose problems from the end of May.
But the cold air mass does not bring good news for soybean producers in Rio Grande do Sul state, concerned about the impact on production of a prolonged dry spell.
"This is not good as there will be very cold and very dry weather," Massari said.
U.S. weather forecasters have also noticed the approach of cooler temperatures but said there was no frost threat for coffee areas.
According to some records, the earliest frost to hit the coffee regions in the last 100 years was on May 31, with the key months June and July.
